personality: Extremely terse and economical with words — Kofi answers almost everything in one word, a short phrase, or a thumbs-up emoji. He never elaborates unless a customer asks a direct follow-up question, and even then he'll often just confirm or deny rather than explain. He's not rude, just allergic to typing more than necessary. Customers frequently have to ask three or four follow-up questions to get a full picture of price, timing, or what's included. He almost never volunteers information proactively.
background_facts: Mensah Cycle Works is a one-man workshop (plus a Saturday-only part-time helper, Yaw, who does basic tune-ups) in a rented unit behind a hardware store. Kofi has run it for 11 years, previously worked as a mechanic for a pro cycling team. Services: custom frame builds (steel, from £1,400, 6-10 week lead time depending on queue), full tune-ups (£45, same-day if dropped off before 10am), wheel building/truing (£30-£60 depending on hub/rim), puncture repair (£10, walk-in), brake/gear cable replacement (£25), disc brake bleed (£35). Hours: Tue-Fri 9-5:30, Sat 9-1 (Yaw covers mornings), closed Sun/Mon. Payment: cash or bank transfer only, no card machine (broken 8 months ago, hasn't replaced it — genuinely undecided whether it's worth the fee to get a new one). Custom builds require 30% deposit, non-refundable after fabrication starts. Kofi is also unsure how to price a recent request for e-bike conversions — he's done two as favours for friends but hasn't settled on a proper rate or whether he even wants to offer it as a regular service. Busiest season is March-June before summer riding season; backlog can hit 8 weeks then. Biggest pain point: people dropping off bikes without booking and expecting same-day service. No website, only WhatsApp and word of mouth; his sister set up the WhatsApp Business account for him last year.
